text: Synthetic/demo frame feeds MUST be lazy (O(1) memory). The edge 'feed --synthetic N' path originally did render_frames(N * [placement]), which materialises N full board images in a list — at N=100000 that's tens of GB and the container silently hangs/OOMs with no logs (feed only prints on completion). Fix: RepeatSource yields one shared image up to count times lazily (count<=0 / None = forever). Watch for the same trap any time a source pre-builds frames.

Supply-chain 7-day seasoning is enforced via [tool.uv] exclude-newer in the WORKSPACE-ROOT pyproject.toml (resolver setting, applies workspace-wide). Set it to today-minus-7-days; uv then resolves only releases published on/before that date (observed: fastapi 0.137->0.136, pytest 9.1->9.0, starlette 1.3->1.2 rolled back). To take newer deps, bump the date deliberately and re-run 'uv sync' + 'uv run pytest'. The Docker build uses 'uv sync --frozen' so images inherit the same seasoned lock.

The edge/inference layer-separation guard must parse imports with AST, not substring-match the source. A naive 'board_reader_edge not in text' check fails because module DOCSTRINGS legitimately mention the forbidden package ('must never import board_reader_edge'). Use ast.walk over Import/ImportFrom nodes and compare top-level package roots.

opencv-python-headless still needs libglib2.0-0 at runtime on python:3.12-slim-bookworm (otherwise import cv2 fails with libgthread/libglib errors). Install it via apt in the image. The 'headless' variant only drops the GUI/X libs, not glib. Viewer image doesn't use cv2 but installing glib there is harmless with the single parametrised Dockerfile.

Edge rectification round-trip accuracy: auto-detection (find_board_quad: Canny->dilate->largest convex quad) leaves a few-pixel corner error, so the un-warped crop correlates ~0.88 with the original (a thin black border sliver). Manual exact corners clear >0.9. Test thresholds set accordingly: auto round-trip 0.85, manual-corners 0.9. Don't tighten the auto bar without improving detection (e.g. Hough-line clustering / sub-pixel corner refinement, DESIGN A1).

The edge Rectifier suppresses output (RectifyResult.crop=None, status recalibrating/needs_setup) during a bump or when no board is locatable, and FileEdgeAdapter.frames() DROPS suppressed frames rather than forwarding them (DESIGN 4.4.1: a mis-localized crop is confidently-wrong geometry, worse for downstream than an honest gap). The L1->L2 wire Frame has NO status field yet, so edge-originated status is not visible to the inference node — it just sees fewer frames. Plumbing status onto the wire / into status events is deferred to M2/M3.

LiteEmbedder (M1 lightweight square embedder) must NOT be a plain grayscale downsample: the synthetic renderer (sim.render_board) draws white pieces as (245,245,245) on light squares (181,217,240; R=240) -> near-zero grayscale contrast -> white-pieces-on-light-squares classify as 'empty' (self-consistency on the start position drops well below 1.0, only ranks 1-2 wrong). Fix that WORKS (100% per-square through the full rectify+crop+embed+classify pipe on synthetic mid-game boards): per-square subtract the median (background) colour, keep the 3 colour channels of the signed deviation (polarity tells white ink + from black ink -), append a tanh-occupancy bias dim so empty squares stay separable under cosine, then L2-normalize. dim = side*side*3 + 1.

Recognition pipeline wiring: the inference gateway selects its Estimator in server._default_estimator() from the BR_CENTROIDS env var (path to a centroids .npz), resolved at IMPORT time so the uvicorn string-imported 'board_reader_inference.server:app' honours 'serve --centroids' without a code change (the CLI sets os.environ before uvicorn.run). Calibrating from the START position yields all 13/13 class centroids in one frame (it contains every class). The embedding backbone is behind the Embedder protocol (embed.py) per DESIGN 4.6 — LiteEmbedder is the synthetic-only stand-in; DINOv2 (onnxruntime) drops into the same seam for real photos. Calibration takes an ALREADY-RECTIFIED crop (inference must not import edge); rectify first with 'board-reader-edge rectify'.

DINOv2->ONNX export (tools/export_dinov2_onnx.py): use OFFICIAL Meta weights facebook/dinov2-small via transformers AutoModel, wrap to return .pooler_output (the 384-d pooled CLS) so the ONNX has a single 'embedding' output. Gotchas with modern torch (2.x, dynamo exporter): (1) needs 'onnxscript' installed or torch.onnx.export raises ModuleNotFoundError; (2) it prints 'Failed to convert to target version 17 ... No Adapter To Version 17 for Resize' — this is a NON-FATAL opset-downconvert warning; the model is still written at a higher opset and runs fine in onnxruntime 1.26; (3) it spills weights to a sidecar 'model.onnx.data' (model.onnx alone is ~1.5MB!) — consolidate with onnx.load then onnx.save_model(save_as_external_data=False) to get one self-contained ~90MB file. Export tooling (torch/transformers/onnx/onnxscript) lives in an ISOLATED uv project OUTSIDE the workspace (../dinov2-export, CPU torch via pytorch-cpu index) so it never bloats the lean inference runtime; runtime only needs onnxruntime. Input pixel_values[batch,3,224,224] ImageNet-normalised RGB, output embedding[batch,384], dynamic batch.

Real-footage M1 validation (yt streams, operator corner-tap): rectification works on real broadcast frames given 4 corners. Recognition (rectify->crop->embed->centroid) WITHIN-frame self-consistency is strong: video1 start 92% piece/100% occ/98% colour; video2 start 98%/100%/100%. BUT lite and dinov2 embedders TIE on self-consistency because calibrate+classify-the-same-frame is a weak test (each square's centroid includes itself) and is permutation-invariant — it does NOT discriminate backbones. To show DINOv2's value you need a SECOND labeled frame (generalization), i.e. the WP-B4 eval harness. GENERALIZATION (calibrate on start, classify a different mid-game frame) is POOR on these clips: the camera is a very low/side broadcast angle, so tall 3D pieces lean almost horizontally and smear across 1-2 neighbouring squares, breaking the per-square independence the flat-plane homography + centroid assumes. This confirms DESIGN's top risk (per-frame accuracy is the binding constraint) and points to needing a better angle, multi-frame burst voting, or piece-height-aware handling (M2+).

Rectified-crop geometry: in a warped top-down crop, pieces smear AWAY from the camera position; the base (true square) is the end of the blob NEAREST the camera side. When labeling ground truth from photos, project the 8x8 grid back onto the ORIGINAL photo (inverse homography) and read base discs there — reading the warped crop misattributes squares by ±1 rank. Also: labels drawn at a cell's crop-space top-left land at the cell's photo-space top-RIGHT when the photo's file axis is mirrored.

DINOv2 few-shot centroid recognition: single-frame calibration transfers poorly across lighting (~70-75%/64 squares across warm-lamp vs daylight photos of the same set); calibrating from frames of BOTH lightings recovers ~90-95%. Gray-world white balance does NOT help (tested). Practical app guidance: calibrate with photos in the lighting you'll use, or accumulate multi-lighting centroids. inset=0.1 beats 0.18/0.25.

models/centroids_dinov2.npz is calibrated from data/eval/img_0565+0566 (Felix's wooden set, both crops + ground-truth FENs in data/eval/ground_truth.json with the operator corner coords). Rebuild with: board-reader-inference calibrate --backbone dinov2. Estimator runs ~3.4s/frame on desktop CPU (64x224x224 DINOv2-S batch).

Few-shot piece recognition: class centroids over DINOv2 embeddings hallucinate pieces on EMPTY squares under lighting shift (LOO on 5 real photos: 28 empty->piece errors, 0 piece->empty). Fix that measured best: keep every calibration crop as a kNN exemplar (nearest-exemplar-per-class), center each board's 64 embeddings by their own mean before cosine (SimpleShot CL2N transductively), box headroom 0.15 (not 0.3), photometric-variant-augmented bank -> 294/320 LOO vs 261, empty->piece 28->6. All kNN voting rules (sum/max/k1/k3/k5) tied - use nearest-exemplar-per-class. Occupancy pre-gate (edge density vs stored empty reference, Chesscog-style) is the documented next lever if hallucinations persist.

crop_squares_photo's per-square sampling geometry (projected quad -> axis-aligned bounding box extended by headroom/side_pad) is now exposed standalone as photo_square_boxes(corners, headroom, side_pad) -> (64,4,2) float32, unclipped. crop_squares_photo itself just clips+pads+resizes those boxes. This is what /estimate?debug=1's diagnostics (draw_boxes/crop_mosaic in diagnostics.py) draw from, so the debug visualization is guaranteed to show the exact geometry recognition used, not a re-derivation.

Vendored chessground 9.2.1 (npm registry tarball, sha1-verified): ships ESM ONLY (no UMD/global build) so it must load via <script type=module> + import; the three CSS files (base/brown/cburnett) embed all piece SVGs as data URIs — no separate assets. Licensing per lila COPYING.md: chessground GPL-3.0+, cburnett pieces GPLv2+ (NOT the CC-BY-SA Wikimedia variant). Chessground needs real layout size — instantiate only after the container is visible (display:none gives a 0x0 board), then update via .set(). cv2.putText is ASCII-only: non-ASCII labels render as '??' (bit us with U+00B7 for empty squares in the debug overlay).

Cross-piece-style transfer does NOT work on frozen DINOv2 features: an exemplar bank built from ChessReD (different physical set) scores 255/320 zero-shot on our photos and a trained linear probe on the same embeddings ties it at 254/320 (vs 294 same-style calibrated) — the gap is in the features, not the classifier (probe hits 90.7% within-ChessReD). Occupancy however IS style-robust (94-96% zero-shot either way), and MIXING styles into one exemplar bank actively hurts (272 vs 291 user-only): wrong-style exemplars win per-class-max matches. Consequence: zero-setup occupancy is free; zero-setup piece-type needs multi-style training data or fine-tuning, not a better classifier on frozen features. ChessReD is CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial), keep out of git.

Server-side relative-path persistence (models/exemplars_session.npz, BR_SAVE_UPLOADS) is a footgun in tests: any test that can trigger a save MUST monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path), or running the suite from the repo root clobbers real user state — this actually happened (a retention test's /calibrate overwrote Felix's real session bank; only the saved upload photos made it rebuildable). Corollary for evals: before using a bank file as a reference, verify its identity (exemplars shape / backbone / box_headroom) — a clobbered 256-row lite-geometry bank silently produced a false 'recognition is broken' conclusion that cost an hour of misdiagnosis.

Dim-room photos (image mean ~37/255) break a daylight-calibrated exemplar bank (~50% start-position accuracy), but appending calibrations taken in the dim conditions fully recovers it: curated daylight bank + 5 dim-light start calibrations = 506/512 on held-out dim start shots. Global exposure normalization (per-photo gamma to mean 110, applied identically at calibration+inference) adds only +2/512 on top of good same-conditions calibration and +13/512 without it — not worth shipping while append-calibration exists. The kNN bank's photometric variants + transductive centering carry most of the lighting robustness.

Start-position auto-calibration (autocalib.py): occupancy is style-robust, and the start position's occupancy pattern (ranks 1,2,7,8 full) is detectable zero-shot (>=60/64 threshold admits 1-2 played moves). Key details: the pattern is 180-degree symmetric so brightness of the occupied bands picks White's side (white pieces brighter in essentially every set); rotation detection also self-corrects 90-degree-off corner labeling WITHOUT re-embedding (crop boxes depend only on the lattice + image-up headroom, so reindexing = rotating the grid); calibration must exclude squares whose occupancy disagrees with the pattern (calib_mask) so post-1.e4 photos or occupancy misreads never contribute mislabeled exemplars. Validated end-to-end on a real dim phone photo: 62/64 match, rotation 0.

Segmentation does NOT fix cross-style piece recognition on frozen DINOv2 features (third independent confirmation of style-entanglement, after kNN-transfer and linear-probe): SAM2-tiny point-prompt masks (visually clean, 1/5440 fallback; point at base-center nudged up 0.3 square-widths — BOX prompts grab the square surface instead of the piece) gave cross-style 255/320 object-centric vs 249 unmasked (within noise), and masking-in-place HURTS (238). Decisive: masking also degrades SAME-style calibrated matching (LOO 291 unmasked vs 280 bbox / 261 in-place), so it is net-negative for the deployed calibration path. Queens/kings still collapse cross-style regardless. Conclusion: the bottleneck is style-entangled features, not background clutter; zero-shot piece-type requires multi-style training data (train on RAW crops, skip SAM at inference).

Classical inference-time embedding alignment cannot close the chess cross-style gap (fourth independent negative on frozen DINOv2): ~50-config sweep (CORAL/whitening-recoloring, ZCA/PCA, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, per-domain z-scoring, top-k PC removal, metric/aggregation swaps) all land within noise of baseline 247/320 (best 252, redistribution not signal). Durable sub-findings: (1) per-class MAX cosine beats nearest-class-mean by ~40 squares — keep MAX in the deployed classifier; (2) CORAL in PCA-mode is pathological (99-158/320, basis mismatch) — if anyone tries CORAL again, ZCA only; (3) style is NOT concentrated in dominant PCs (removing k>=2 monotonically degrades). Cross-style piece-type needs supervised signal, period.

Published pretrained chess recognizers, zero-shot on our 5 real photos (320 sq, GT corners, each project's own crop geometry): LiveChess2FEN Xception 256/320 (80%) — on par with our cross-style DINOv2 kNN (249-255), strong on empty/pawns but non-pawn piece types collapse to 'pawn' (r→p, R→P top confusions); chesscog official weights 151/320 (their paper itself says 2-photo fine-tune is required for a new set). Nobody's published single-style-trained model beats our same-style calibrated 294/320. Gotcha for anyone reusing chesscog code: warp_chessboard_image() calls sort_corner_points() which SILENTLY re-derives corner order from pixel positions, discarding semantic a8/h8/h1/a1 order — bypass it or orientation flips. Net: independent confirmation that style-diverse training is the missing ingredient, not architecture.

The session-bank clobber hazard RECURRED through a new feature: the calibrated-path auto-refresh made plain /estimate calls write models/exemplars_session.npz, so a pre-existing photo-mode test (never a writer before) clobbered the real bank from a repo-root pytest run — and this time the server restarted onto the clobbered file, silently serving garbage (lite 769-dim bank under a dinov2 server; symptom: confidence ~0.27 on photos that should read 0.87+). Per-test chdir sandboxing does NOT scale as a defense: any future test can become a writer when a feature adds a persistence side effect. Structural fix shipped: ALL session persistence/restore is opt-in via BR_SESSION_BANK env (unset = in-memory only, nothing written ever), plus a guard test asserting no npz lands on disk without opt-in. Ops lesson: after any server restart, verify a KNOWN photo reads at expected confidence, not just healthz.

In the snapshot page (and any DOM UI): never use a live element.contains(ev.target) check inside a bubbled document-level click handler when an inner handler may rebuild that subtree's innerHTML — the clicked node is detached by the time the event bubbles, contains() returns false, and the handler misfires (here: the correction panel closed on every direct grid pick). Use ev.composedPath() (captured at dispatch) instead. Found by fresh-context review of a 500k-context author's code — pairing a long-context author with a fresh reviewer catches exactly this class of bug.

NEVER pause CUDA training with SIGSTOP/SIGCONT: after resume the process can become a zombie-spinner — GPU pegged at 100% util while actual throughput collapses ~30x (observed: 300 steps in 18 min pre-freeze, 140 steps in 4.9h post-resume, zero epochs completed). Liveness checks and nvidia-smi both look healthy, so ONLY a throughput monitor (steps/min from the log) catches it. Pause GPU training via checkpoint+kill+resume-from-checkpoint instead. Related: on Turing (GTX 1650) scaler-less fp16 autocast overflows to NaN (use GradScaler — that's its whole job) and bf16 is emulated (slow), so fp16+GradScaler is the fast path.

CORRECTION to the Turing AMP learning (85aab09c98c4): fp16+GradScaler is NOT the fix on the GTX 1650 — measured 0/30 finite steps (the NaN is in the FORWARD pass logits, which GradScaler cannot address; it only rescales the backward), and fp16 ran 0.78 steps/s vs fp32's 2.63 (this card hits a slow fp16 route, not tensor cores). Measured hierarchy on GTX 1650 + torch 2.12+cu130, resnet18 bs~64: fp32 2.63 steps/s > bf16 0.99 (emulated) > fp16 0.78 (and NaN). Use plain fp32 on this card. Also: a wedged CUDA zombie can survive kill -9 on the PID (futex wait) — kill the process GROUP (kill -9 -PGID).

Frozen-backbone bakeoff (fixed kNN protocol, ChessReD bank -> user photos): NO off-the-shelf encoder reaches zero-shot piece-type; best = DINOv2-S with CENTRAL-COLUMN patch-token pooling (mean of middle 8/16 token columns) at 256/320 cross-style with near-perfect occupancy (0 p->e, 2 e->p) — +9 over CLS pooling on the same backbone, the one transferable win (candidate app improvement: swap CLS->central-column pooling, requires ONNX re-export + bank rebuild). Scale does nothing (S 247 -> B 250). Shape-biased SIN-ResNet50 REFUTED instructively: best same-style of all (296/320) but WORST cross-style (219/320) — shape bias over-specializes to same-set silhouettes instead of generalizing. SigLIP2/OpenCLIP image towers mediocre both ways. Failure is entirely piece TYPE (R/N/B/Q/K recall 0.0-0.4 cross-style; empty 0.99, pawns ~0.8).

Deploying a trained crop-classifier: the winning verification chain was (1) a trainer-produced FIXTURE (4 PNG crops + expected logits through the exact training preprocessing) proving the server-side preprocess reproduces training bit-for-bit (caught nothing this time only because the contract was written down first — RGB vs BGR, outside-graph ImageNet normalization, NCHW, raw logits in CLASSES order), (2) full eval through the DEPLOYED estimator class matching the training-side eval exactly (296/320), (3) live known-photo read. TrainedEstimator seam: crop_mode='photo' on the ESTIMATOR (no classifier attr) — server's _photo_estimator checks both. Precedence BR_CENTROIDS > BR_MODEL > session-restore > stub; /calibrate still swaps a bank over the trained model (covers the dim-light regime where per-set banks still win).

Crop headroom is load-bearing for piece-type accuracy at steep camera angles: headroom=0.15 (near-base-only crops) makes tall pieces read as shorter ones (q→b, K→Q, R→P, B→P) and their cut-off heads hallucinate pawns one square up (field 2026-07-18: 57/64 with every major piece wrong on a steep dim shot). crop_squares_photo's image-space upward extension (default 1.6) exists for exactly this; the 0.15 came from the kNN era and silently became the trained pipeline's geometry. Train and serve must share crop geometry, so fixing headroom means a retrain, not a config flip.

Calibration must boost, not replace, the trained zero-shot model: the kNN exemplar bank is near-perfect under conditions it has seen (64/64 on bank-adjacent boards) but collapses outside them (46/64 on a steep+dim shot); the trained model is the reverse. A 50/50 square_dist blend (EnsembleEstimator) tracks the better member square-by-square: 439/448 vs 415 (trained) / 430 (bank) on the 7-board eval. Horizontal-flip TTA on the trained model actively hurts (415→409) — don't add it.

Never use square-color parity or printed border coordinates to resolve board orientation: players set boards up ignoring printed coords, and non-FIDE-printed boards exist (both observed in one 2026-07-18 field session — a position played 90° to the printed grid, and a shot where parity would have 'corrected' a correct orientation). Chess-content plausibility works instead: fewest pawns on ranks 1/8, tie-broken by White's piece mass nearer rank 1 (autocalib.resolve_rotation). Only auto-rotate when the operator has NOT hand-placed/relabeled corners — their labeling is authoritative.

The test suite loads the DINOv2 ONNX with the CUDA provider whenever the GPU is visible — during GPU-owned training runs this fails with BFCArena OOM (transient, looks like a code regression but isn't). When the GPU is busy, run tests as CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" uv run pytest. Extends the single-owner-GPU rule to the test suite.

Bank-corruption incident #3 (2026-07-18 16:23): /calibrate trusted the operator's corner orientation, but with auto-detected corners + server-side autorotate the user never SEES that corners are 180° off — their calibrate tap then pushes color-swapped exemplars into the persisted bank (White labeled Black), and every subsequent ensembled read shows color-flips. Fix: /calibrate probes the photo with the stateless trained member (cannot be poisoned) and rotates the claimed labels to best agreement (accept only if best beats as-given by ≥8 squares); recovery: tools/rebuild_session_bank.py rebuilds from base + all retained calibrate uploads with the same verification (it caught exactly the one poisoned calibrate, agree=[32,19,56,20]). General rule: any UI affordance that silently corrects a user-visible error (autorotate) can mask the same error from flows that still trust it (calibrate) — audit label-trusting paths when adding auto-correction.

Field incident #4 + operating envelope: at projected board aspect (corner-quad short/long side) below ~0.6 the camera is nearly level with the board, pieces occlude whole ranks, and recognition goes near-random (measured h/w 0.56: garbage; 0.73+: usable). Server warns with 'very_low_angle' below 0.62 (_quad_aspect in server.py). ALSO: users tap Calibrate on whatever is on the board (a mid-game position got calibrated as 'start', poisoning the bank a second time) — /calibrate now rejects when <60% of the CLAIMED PIECE squares agree with a stateless probe (empty squares excluded from the metric: mid-game vs start share an empty middle, inflating whole-board agreement to ~40/64 and masking the mismatch). Whole-board agreement is the wrong metric for placement verification; piece-square agreement is the right one.

The inference server SQUATS 2.1GB of GPU when serving the ensemble: the DINOv2 embedder ONNX session successfully takes CUDAExecutionProvider even though the trained-model session fails over to CPU (missing libcublasLt) — so 'the server is CPU-only' was silently false after the ensemble deploy, and it would have OOM'd the next training launch (4GB card, lc0 holds 1GB, training needs 2.9GB). During training campaigns serve with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" — CPU reads are 0.6s/board, indistinguishable for the phone flow. Check nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps after ANY server restart; the single-owner-GPU rule includes our own long-running services.

Headroom sweep verdict (2026-07-18): tall crops hr1.6/sp0.15 are the deployed geometry — same recipe/data as hr0.15 gave vlab 0.665→0.835 and user photos 415→430/448 alone; hr1.8/sp0.25 ties the holdout but LOSES on real photos (409) — more context ≠ better, 1.6 is the sweet spot. Ensemble weight should follow bank maturity: mature bank (≥1024 exemplars) earns 30/70 trained/bank (633/640) while 50/50 regressed a start photo (tall crops occasionally color-flip backlit pawns; the mature bank outvotes them). Geometry ships with the model via <model>.onnx.meta.json.

Board-reader eval contamination (found 2026-08-06): the session exemplar bank's base is models/exemplars_dinov2.npz, built by tools/build_exemplar_bank.py FROM data/eval/ground_truth.json — so the deployed ensemble is scored on boards whose own crops are in the bank. Symptom: bank scores 64/64 on 9/10 eval boards and 43/64 on up_20260718_0001, the single board it never saw. The 633/640 (98.9%) headline is therefore train-on-test; the honest generalization number is the trained model alone at 605/640 with only 2/10 PERFECT boards. Always report perfect-board rate alongside per-square accuracy: at 94.5% per-square a 64-square board averages ~3.5 wrong squares, so per-square looks great while whole-board recognition essentially never succeeds. Any new eval set must be disjoint from the calibration bank.

onnxruntime-gpu wheels from PyPI are built against CUDA 12, so on a system with CUDA 13 (no libcublasLt.so.12) the CUDA EP fails to load and ORT silently falls back to CPU. The CUDA 12 libs are usually already in the venv as nvidia-*-cu12 wheels, just not on the loader path: call ort.preload_dlls() before the first InferenceSession (board_reader_inference.onnxrt.cuda_providers does this) instead of setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH at the launcher.

The deployed crop classifier is models/d16/model.onnx; compose.yaml and docs/runbook.md are the source of truth for BR_MODEL. models/piece_classifier_multistyle_v1.onnx is superseded but still on disk and still loads — it has no .onnx.meta.json sidecar, so TrainedEstimator falls back to v1's headroom=0.15 short-crop geometry. Serving tall-crop weights on that geometry produces the decapitation signature: back-rank kings read as bishops plus phantom pawns on the rank in front. Check the stderr sidecar warning before trusting a bad read.

Snapshot page: never size the photo canvas with percentage max-height through an auto-height ancestor — a percentage max-height resolves against an indefinite height, is treated as 'none', and lets a portrait photo overflow (visibly clipped by the frame's overflow:hidden). Size the canvas in JS (fitPhoto: k = min(box.w/src.w, box.h/src.h)) and re-run it from a ResizeObserver on the frame, because the row re-flows whenever the piece switcher opens/closes beside the board — a one-shot fit on load leaves a stale size behind. renderHandles() must run again after every refit, since corner handles are positioned in CSS px off the canvas rect.

Ground truth must be stored in the frame the photo's corners define, never as displayed. The snapshot page shows an autorotated board (resolve_rotation applies k quarter-turns via np.rot90(dist,k,axes=(0,1))); POST /labels undoes that turn before writing, so a label never inherits a model output and survives a model whose orientation guess differs. A label whose upload has no corners is refused (422) — a placement with no frame is data no eval can replay.

Per-square accuracy is the wrong headline for board reading: 94.5%/square = ~3.5 wrong squares = an unusable position. Measured 2026-08-06 with board-reader-inference eval on the 10 curated boards: trained d16 alone 605/640 but only 2/10 perfect; deployed ensemble 633/640 and 7/10 perfect, where the +5 is the bank recognising its own exemplars (its base is built FROM data/eval/ground_truth.json). Confidence is unusable at board level — trained model averages 0.957 on perfect boards and 0.958 on wrong ones. Ensemble is the opposite failure: under-confident everywhere, ECE 0.130, because blending two distributions flattens the peak even when both members agree.

Model A/B on this project must be run as the ENSEMBLE (BR_MODEL + BR_SESSION_BANK through board-reader-inference eval), not model-alone via tools/train/evaluate.py: run_e vs d16 flipped verdict between the two. Alone, run_e loses the bright eval set (599 vs 605/640, 0/10 vs 2/10 perfect); ensembled it wins outright (638/640, 9/10 perfect vs 633, 7/10) and also wins the single uncontaminated board up_20260718_0001 (62/64 vs 59/64). Ensembling is what serves, so the alone-number is the wrong gate. Also: the 12 dim -calibrate uploads are NOT visible to the eval harness (they carry -calibrate.json sidecars, not .label.json) and are all start positions, so perfect-board rate is meaningless on that slice -- score it per-square via a throwaway loader, and use models/exemplars_dinov2.npz (built only from data/eval) as the bank there since the session bank contains those 12 boards.

Probing a running server with BR_SESSION_BANK pointed at a path that does not YET exist causes the server to bootstrap-calibrate from the first /estimate photo and WRITE a fresh small bank there (252 exemplars vs the real 4096) -- copy the bank into place BEFORE launching, since the estimator is resolved at startup and a later cp is ignored while the write-back still fires. Tell-tale: identical confidence with and without a bank means you are serving trained-alone. Also, never pkill/pgrep on a pattern like 'port 8123' from inside a Bash tool call -- it matches the wrapping zsh -c command string and kills your own shell (exit 144), leaving the real uvicorn alive holding ~2.8GB of the 4GB GPU; the next ORT session then dies with a BFCArena allocation failure that looks like a model bug. Kill by PID from 'ps -eo pid,args'.

Reindexing an 8x8 board lattice by np.rot90(.,k) is exactly a +k cyclic shift of the ordered corner quad (C'[i]=C[(i+k)%4], a8/h8/h1/a1) -- BUT only for the lattice itself. photo_square_boxes' headroom (upward) and side_pad (sideways) extend each box along FIXED IMAGE axes, so re-deriving boxes from shifted corners silently rotates those extensions too and samples the wrong pixels on a 90/270 turn (~0.26px at headroom=0.2, ~0.77px at 0.6, ~0.19px from side_pad=0.15 alone). The two agree exactly only when BOTH padding params are 0, or at 180deg -- which is why a quick check with headroom=side_pad=0 looks reassuring and is wrong in the field. To keep /estimate's ?debug=1 boxes/mosaic in step with an autorotated square_dist, sample from the ORIGINAL corners (what recognition actually saw) and permute the resulting arrays with the identical np.rot90 -- an exact index permutation, immune to padding.

Any test that exercises a quarter-turn rotation MUST cover 90 or 270 degrees, never only 180: np.rot90(x,2) == np.rot90(x,-2), so a 180-only test passes unchanged when the rotation direction is inverted -- the exact bug class such a test exists to catch. Verified by mutation: flipping rotate_k to -rotate_k in server._debug_payload left the 180 case green while 90/270 failed. Parametrize over (1,270),(2,180),(3,90). Forcing a specific turn end-to-end is easy: render a board whose placement is rot90(P,k0) and autocalib.resolve_rotation reliably picks k=(4-k0)%4 to put it upright (confirmed for all four k0 on a normal mid-game position).

Server-side autorotation must be ADOPTED by the snapshot page, not just displayed. /estimate?autorotate=1 returns square_dist/placement as rot90(corner-frame grid,k) with ev.autorotated=k*90; if the page leaves its own label rotation alone it holds two orientations at once -- board correct, but corner handles, corner table, client rectified preview and the per-square crop thumbnail all still describe the pre-rotation frame (reported symptom: 'position is correct but corners are misaligned and the crop shows the wrong square'). Fix: rot -= k on a FRESH read only, then draw()+maybeRectify() with no re-read. Guard on restored===null -- a history entry stored the rot it was rendered with, so absorbing again double-rotates. Keep cornersEdited FALSE (corners are still auto-detected, so later reads keep asking for autorotation). Ground truth is unaffected: /labels undoes the sidecar's recorded autorotated against the POSTED corner order, which is independent of what the page displays -- verified end-to-end (stored truth rotated +k reproduces the displayed placement exactly).

Verifying the snapshot page end-to-end without touching real user data: seed a scratch dir with a handful of copied data/uploads photos (jpg + json sidecar + any .label.json), then run 'BR_MODEL=models/run_e/model.onnx BR_SAVE_UPLOADS=<scratch> board-reader-inference serve' with BR_SESSION_BANK DELIBERATELY UNSET -- session persistence is opt-in, so nothing is ever written to the real bank, and new reads land in the scratch dir instead of polluting the eval corpus. Then 'BR_INFERENCE_HTTP=http://localhost:8000 board-reader-viewer --port 8080' and drive /snapshot with Playwright. Page internals are module-scoped (not on window), so assert via the DOM instead: corner-handle textContent+style.left/top recovers pts and rot exactly (labelOf(i)=CORNER_ORDER[(i+rot)%4]), and #cpCrop's computed background-position identifies which mosaic tile the inspector is showing. Kill the servers by PID from 'ps -eo pid,args' -- never pkill on a pattern.

Confirm-as-read labels are not independent ground truth. 11 of the first 13 snapshot labels were saved with corrections:0 — the operator agreed with the answer the page was already displaying. Any square where operator and model are both wrong scores as correct, so an eval built from them is an upper bound on the exact estimator that produced them (measured 823/832 for the deployed ensemble). To get real truth, read the position off the board or the source video BEFORE looking at the overlay; the corrections count in the label file is the only signal of how blind the pass was.

Bank writes are not monotone — calibrating can cost squares on boards that already read perfectly. Upload 20260806-231719-0000 read 64/64 live, was confirmed as-read, and after two later /calibrate writes re-scored 63/64 (e6 empty->p) while the trained model alone still got it right, so the added exemplars caused it. Nothing evaluates a bank write before it lands. When comparing an eval run against what a board did live, check the bank mtime first: a bank that moved between the read and the score is a different estimator.

labels._boards_from_ground_truth silently skips curated entries whose source image is gone, so the eval set shrinks without an error. Five of data/eval/ground_truth.json's ten boards point at deleted data/uploads photos, which is why the historical 638/640 baseline can no longer be reproduced — the harness just reports fewer boards. data/ and models/ are both gitignored, so nothing about the eval corpus is version-controlled. Check the reported board count against what the file claims before comparing any run to a past number.

An ONNX 'BFC arena failed to allocate' RuntimeException from the eval/CLI usually means the GPU is full, not RAM: _onnx_logits_fn uses cuda_providers(), and a dev server left running holds ~2.8GB of the 4GB GTX 1650, so a second process dies on a 50MB MaxPool buffer while host RSS sits under 1GB. Either stop the server or run the CLI with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= to force CPU (it falls back loudly but works).

`kill 0` inside a shell trap segfaults bash: the process group includes the trap shell itself, so the group kill re-enters its own TERM trap, which kills the group again, recursing until the stack overflows. `make dev`'s teardown was `trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM`, so every Ctrl-C exited 139 and dumped a 1.9MB core while the servers themselves shut down cleanly. Kill children by captured PID instead, and have the handler run `trap - EXIT INT TERM` first so it cannot re-enter regardless.

Attribute a segfault with `coredumpctl info <pid>` before blaming the native ML deps. When `make dev` died with 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)' the plausible culprit was onnxruntime/opencv teardown at interpreter exit, but the dump named /usr/bin/bash as the executable and showed a run_pending_traps recursion — the Python servers had logged a clean 'Finished server process' first. The dump's Command Line field also identifies which shell/recipe it was.

`uv run` forwards SIGTERM to the process it spawns, so killing the uv PID gives uvicorn a graceful shutdown — no need for a process-group kill or to hunt down the python grandchild PID. Verified against board-reader-viewer: kill the uv pid, the child logs 'Waiting for application shutdown' through 'Finished server process' and leaves no orphan.

A two-process dev target must use `wait -n`, not bare `wait`: bare wait blocks until both exit, so if the inference server dies at startup (port already bound) the viewer keeps serving a dead backend and the recipe still exits 0. `wait -n` returns on the first exit, letting the target tear down the survivor and propagate the real status.

'The data is broken' is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis. chesscog_transfer was retired for weeks as a 'geometrically broken' holdout (frozen-DINOv2 self-kNN 0.597, made a good run look like a 0.50 failure). The crops and corners were fine — all 22 warps grid-align. What was broken: build_transfer_labels.py resolved each photo's orientation BY EYE (WHITE_NEAR dict) and got it wrong on 14 of 22 boards, rotating every label 180 degrees; 2 more boards were SILENT detect_board_quad failures (a quad of the table, not the board). Repaired photometrically (repair_orientation.py): checkerboard parity of EMPTY cells fixes the 90-degree ambiguity (a8 must be light), light-vs-dark piece wood fixes the 180 one, each cell read against the median of empty cells sharing its square colour so the checkerboard cancels. run_e (never trained on it) goes 0.500 -> 0.819. Two independent methods (photometric + trained model) agreed board-for-board. Lesson: when a metric says a dataset is bad, it localises a problem but not its LAYER — check geometry and labels separately.

A per-image ambiguity resolved by eye needs an EXHAUSTIVE check, not a spot check. chesscog_transfer's original README claimed 'No mislabels observed' after inspecting a mosaic of 4 test images — three of the fourteen broken boards simply weren't in the sample, and the set was then trusted for weeks. If a labelling step has a per-item free choice (orientation, which side is White), validate every item and report a NUMBER (here: parity and piece-colour margins per board, decisive at >=+92 and >=+37 grey levels on kept boards, ~0 on the 2 failures). Related: cropcache's staleness check compares only n_samples and size, so labels whose CONTENT changed without changing the board COUNT would silently reuse a stale cache.

torch 2.12's DEFAULT onnx exporter (dynamo path) silently ignores dynamic_axes and bakes the export-time batch in as a CONSTANT. Symptom is nasty: the export succeeds, the assert on output shape passes at batch 1, and it dies only on the first real batch with a reshape error from deep inside the backbone ('Input shape:{64,257,384}, requested shape:{257,384}', node gemm_input_reshape) — pointing at the model's own internals, not at your wrapper. Pass dynamo=False to pin the legacy TorchScript exporter, which honours dynamic_axes. Also: inside a wrapper module reshape with -1 for batch (tokens.reshape(-1, g, g, c)), never a traced tokens.shape[0]. Second gotcha from the same export: the legacy exporter may leave the output width SYMBOLIC ('ReduceMeanembedding_dim_1'), so int(session.get_outputs()[0].shape[-1]) raises ValueError on a perfectly good model — resolve the dim by probing with one dummy input instead (DinoV2Embedder._resolve_dim). A board is 64 crops and calibration hands over hundreds, so batch-1-only is fatal, not cosmetic.

Temperature scaling of the deployed ensemble WORKS, and the metric you judge it by decides whether you notice. Measured leave-one-board-out on 23 labelled boards (run_e + session bank): ECE 0.255 -> 0.004, T=0.251 and remarkably stable across folds (0.235-0.257, which is itself the evidence the parameter is real and not fitting noise), answers changed 0. BUT the perfect/imperfect board-confidence GAP collapses +0.136 -> +0.017, which reads as 'the separation died' — it did not: board ranking AUC goes 0.862 -> 0.877. The gap shrinks because scaling squeezes everything toward 1.0; only a RANK-based statistic (Mann-Whitney AUC) survives a monotone squeeze, so report AUC alongside any confidence-gap claim. Implementation notes: the estimator emits probabilities not logits (an ensemble averages distributions), so scale as q ∝ p^(1/T) == softmax(log p / T); argmax is invariant for all T>0, so this can never change a published placement; fit by golden-section over log T (no scipy needed); and fit LEAVE-ONE-BOARD-OUT or the number grades itself.

Pose-aware crop geometry (PoseGeometry) vs the scalar-headroom bbox: you do NOT have to guess the focal length. Zhang's two plane-homography constraints (b1.b2=0 and |b1|=|b2| where b=K^-1 h) each solve for f^2 in closed form; take the better-conditioned one, and fall back to a focal_ratio assumption only when the view is near top-down (H's third row -> 0, which genuinely carries no information about f). Recover r1,r2,t straight from the homography (do NOT SVD-orthonormalise all three) so the Z=0 plane reproduces the existing base quads EXACTLY and only the height is new; get r3 = normalize(cross(r1,r2)) and sign it by solving M w = -t and requiring w[2]>0 (camera above the table). Measured effect on a real angled photo: box height near/far ratio 1.57 (bbox, tracks foreshortened square WIDTH) -> 1.15 (pose, tracks real piece height). Bonus property worth knowing: pose boxes re-derived from rotated corner labels EQUAL the rot90 of the originals, because a prism stands along the board normal which relabelling cannot move — the exact property bbox geometry provably lacks (its extension follows fixed IMAGE axes), which is why the autorotate debug path had to reindex rather than re-derive.

GTX 1650 training throughput is COMPUTE-bound at ~165 img/s (fp32 resnet18@224): measured flat across batch 48/64/96 (163/166/170 img/s), workers 6/8/12 (168/163/169) — the JPEG-decode+augment loader keeps up, so don't chase dataloader tuning on this box. channels_last actively HURTS (136 img/s, no fp32 NHWC kernels on Turing) and torch.compile is unavailable (system python 3.14, no triton packaged). Real wall-time wins on this card: patience/early-stop, and a 2x batch for the val pass (no backward -> ~free; val was ~40% of epoch wall time at holdout size 16k). Peak VRAM at bs96 is only ~250 MiB — memory is never the constraint here, kernels are.

Run observability contract (train.py): every run dir has four synchronized views — val.log (tail -f), events.jsonl (JSONL meta/step/epoch/abort/end; step records carry loss, lr, imgs_per_s, gpu_mem_mib — imgs_per_s is the liveness signal that catches zombie-spinners), history.json (rewritten each epoch, crash-safe, val includes the full 13x13 confusion), and curves/diagnostics/confusion PNGs re-rendered per epoch by plots.py (also a standalone CLI that works on pre-instrumentation runs). Runs abort immediately on non-finite loss with an 'abort' event saying where. Checkpoints save the EAGER module's state_dict (eager_model ref kept before torch.compile wraps) so keys never grow the _orig_mod. prefix.

Python 3.14 changed the multiprocessing default start method from fork to forkserver, which turns DataLoader workers from copy-on-write sharers into full PICKLED COPIES of the dataset — with the ~9 GB RAM-resident JPEG StyleData that meant 8 workers x 9 GB and the kernel OOM-killed the first run_f launch ('pickle data was truncated' in the traceback is the tell). Fix: pass multiprocessing_context='fork' to DataLoader (workers never touch CUDA, so fork-after-CUDA-init is safe); verified via /proc/<worker>/smaps_rollup — Rss 1.0 GB but Pss 160 MB, i.e. ~85% shared. Also: pick_device's silent CPU fallback when the GPU is busy would have turned the 45-min run into days — it now aborts instead (set device: cpu to force).

The training harness MUST run under scratch/torchvenv (the driver scripts now default PY to it). /usr/bin/python looks viable — it has CUDA torch and trains fine — but has no onnx/onnxscript/onnxruntime, so export.py and evaluate.py die AFTER the GPU time is spent. From torch 2.9 on, torch.onnx.export routes through the dynamo exporter and imports onnxscript, so onnxscript is a hard requirement, not optional. tools/train/_env.sh preflights the interpreter before any GPU work; do not bypass it.

Shrinking the training set does NOT make runs faster. steps_per_epoch (300) x batch_size (48) = 14,400 images per epoch out of 663,680 — 2.2%, or 0.43 passes over the corpus across a full 20-epoch run. Wall clock is set by epochs, by the val set (16,000 crops = ~25% of each epoch, capped via val_max), and by image size. max_boards only helps the one-off cropcache build for a NEW geometry. Use screen.sh for a ~13-min ranking tier; it cannot produce a deployable number because the curve climbs to ~e17.

Early-stop patience below ~8 truncates real runs on this task. The LOSO curve keeps climbing to about epoch 17 (run_e: e6 0.835, e11 0.880, e17 0.898) with multi-epoch stalls on the way — run_e stalled 3 epochs at e8-e10, and run_f's first attempt died at e8 on a 4-epoch stall having peaked at 0.847, answering nothing. On a 40-minute run patience saves almost no compute, so set it wide; screen.sh disables it outright.

Never compare a new run against a baseline's on-disk eval.txt — re-run evaluate.py on the baseline's .onnx with current code and data first. run_e's eval.txt is from 19 Jul, predates the chesscog_transfer repair, and covers a different board set (22 vs 32) because curated photos have since been deleted. The re-eval lives at scratch/runs/run_e/eval_rerun.txt. Each model is scored with its OWN geometry sidecar, so bbox and pose runs are comparable this way.

Edge motion meter (motion.py): downscaling to a 32x32 INTER_AREA thumbnail averages ~56 source pixels per cell, so the mean abs inter-frame difference comes out far smaller than a naive full-res estimate predicts — a bright hand-sized block (11% of frame area, ~0.29 intensity delta) yields d~0.026, not ~0.05. The exp(-gain*d) curve therefore needs gain~80, not ~25, for a hand sweep to score well below 0.5 in one frame. Calibrate the gain against measured thumbnail diffs, never against full-res arithmetic.

ONNX InferenceSession creation (DINOv2 embed tests) can fail with BFCArena 'Failed to allocate memory' errors under machine-wide memory pressure — e.g. several concurrent agent/pytest/uvicorn processes. It presents as a deterministic-looking test-ordering bug (cv2-heavy boarddetect tests then test_embed in one process) but is load-sensitive: the same pair passes when the machine quiets down. Before blaming new code, re-run on a clean worktree of HEAD (symlink models/ and data/ in — they are git-ignored, and without them @requires_dinov2 silently skips and the repro is void).

Rectifier cadence (redetect_interval_s, M2): between cadence ticks frames ride the cached homography UNEXAMINED — a frame with no locatable board (blank/occluded) is happily warped into a confident crop. Detection-dependent behaviours (needs_setup suppression, bump recovery) only fire on tick frames, or every frame after a failed detection (a miss never advances the cadence). Tests asserting per-frame suppression must pass redetect_interval_s=0 or omit ts. The adapter meters motion on the RAW frame and rectifies only forwarder-approved frames, so dropped frames never pay the ~90-100 ms detection cost.

The DINOv2 test_embed flake is GPU memory contention, not system RAM: onnxruntime's CUDA EP fails InferenceSession init / kernels with 'BFCArena Failed to allocate memory' when other processes hold the GTX 1650's 4GB (concurrent agent sessions, a running serve, training). Proof: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run pytest packages/inference/tests/test_embed.py passes while the same tests fail with CUDA visible. It masquerades as a test-ordering bug and comes and goes with GPU load. Before blaming new code: re-run with CUDA hidden, and check nvidia-smi for squatters.

ffmpeg SILENTLY CLAMPS an out-of-range crop instead of failing: crop=w:h:x:y with y+h past the frame height produces a correctly-sized image shifted to fit, with no warning and exit 0. A stale or mis-recorded crop row therefore shifts every extracted frame undetectably. Found in this repo: the coffeechess row had y=435 with h=310 on a 720-tall frame (745>720); ffmpeg had actually used y=410, which is what the on-disk frames show. tools/video/streams.py now validates the crop against frame_width/frame_height at load time so the row is rejected rather than quietly reinterpreted.

detect_board_quad is NOT usable to locate the board in a full broadcast frame. Measured on 6 real 720p/1080p frames: outright failure on 3, and on a 4th it confidently returned a perfectly axis-aligned SQUARE quad that was the broadcast's 2D overlay board, not the physical one. On already-cropped frames it works fine. Two consequences: (a) the capture workflow must be crop-first (manual), detect-second; (b) a returned quad with aspect ~1.000 and zero perspective on a broadcast frame is a strong overlay-board false-positive signature worth checking for.

A lost crop row is recoverable from any surviving extracted frame: cv2.matchTemplate(full_frame_at_t, extracted_frame, TM_CCOEFF_NORMED) returns correlation 1.0 at the exact (x,y), because the frames were cut losslessly from that video. Recovered 62h7O9Ns_eA as x=606,y=594 (748x396 @1920x1080), confirmed at two independent timestamps. The extracted frame's filename timestamp is the absolute time in the SOURCE video, which is what makes re-extracting the matching full frame possible.

Table-level chess broadcast cameras are mostly OUTSIDE the reader's operating envelope. Gating 5 absorbed broadcasts on median projected board aspect (quad_aspect over detect_board_quad, floor 0.62) rejected 4: 0.445, 0.450, 0.508, 0.573; the sole survivor measured 0.650, i.e. 'degraded', still below the 0.73 band every good result was measured in. Producers shoot low and wide for the room. Treat a steeper/overhead source as a sourcing requirement when collecting broadcast test data, and angle-gate BEFORE extracting a batch of frames. Detections within one broadcast are near-identical (fixed camera), so a median over ~10 frames is a trustworthy per-stream measurement.

Chessground TAKES OVER the element you hand it: Chessground(el, cfg) adds .cg-wrap to el itself and sizes cg-container from el's box. So a descendant rule like '.board .cg-wrap { width:100%; height:100% }' is dead CSS (snapshot.html only needs it because it wraps #board in a separate .board-wrap). In the live viewer the element passed in IS sized directly (explicit px via --board-size), and it must already have real size at construction time — hence appendChild(card) BEFORE Chessground(). Its autoShapes brushes render as: yellow=#e68f00 opacity 1, green=#15781B opacity 1, paleGreen=#15781B opacity 0.4 — so green -> paleGreen -> removed is a real fade driven entirely by the page's existing ticker, with zero per-event timers.

Verifying the LIVE viewer page (index.html) end-to-end needs a real model: with BR_MODEL unset the inference node runs the walking-skeleton FixedEstimator, which emits START_PLACEMENT for every frame regardless of pixels — so per-square confidence is uniform and the placement NEVER changes, and no change-flash / low-confidence marker can ever fire no matter what the edge streams. Run 'BR_MODEL=models/run_e/model.onnx uv run board-reader-inference serve --port

' with BR_SESSION_BANK DELIBERATELY UNSET (calibration then stays in-memory and cannot poison the real bank) plus 'board-reader-edge feed --game --loop --throttle --adaptive'; the model misreads the synthetic ASCII board badly, which is fine and in fact ideal — it produces constantly changing placements and plenty of low-confidence squares. Note --game WITHOUT --loop --throttle sends its 208 frames in a couple of seconds and exits, leaving the card stale. Also: 'uv run X' forks a child in .venv/bin — killing the 'uv run' pid alone leaves the server bound to its port; kill the .venv child pid too (find both via ps, never pkill on a pattern).
